title: Wie geht es?
desc: There is a whole scale under this
setting: An office in Kriens in February, sixteen days of fog, and a colleague who has stopped typing.

options.feedback: Two words and the whole afternoon changes. Es geht is the answer that says: ask again.
The greeting with more words in it. Nothing wrong with it and nothing happens after it.
The bottom of the scale. It is honest and it is a lot to hand somebody at ten in the morning.
Small and true. He will not push and he will know exactly what you mean, because he has it too.
He turned round in his chair for this. Kompliziert sends him back to the screen.

options.es: Alles. Ich weiss nicht mehr, was ich hier mache.
options.en: Everything. I do not know what I am doing here any more.
options.feedback: That is the real answer. It is also more than the question was built to carry, and he will listen anyway.

steps.speaker: Marco
steps.es: Ja. Der Februar ist der schlimmste.

options.feedback: Ask. The useful part is not the sympathy, it is finding out that everybody here is like this in February.
He was not asking to be reassured. He was telling you something, and it was the useful thing.

options.es: Ich dachte, das liegt an mir.
options.en: I thought it was just me.
options.feedback: Honest, and it is why he said it. Alle sind so is the whole medicine here.
One word. With him that is the entire language for this and anything longer would spoil it.
He knows. Refusing a small kindness here makes the other person carry it back.

options.en: Say nothing and get back to work.
options.feedback: Fine, and a merci costs nothing. He brought it across the room.
